title: Rider, Elephant, or Path?
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Classify nine change tactics as directing the rider, motivating the elephant, or shaping the path, the three parts of the Switch framework.

learningObjectives: The learner will classify nine change tactics as directing the rider, motivating the elephant, or shaping the path, correctly placing at least eight of nine on the first attempt.
prerequisites: The Switch framework, direct the rider, motivate the elephant, shape the path, and the nine tactics, from the section "The Switch Framework" in Chapter 19.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Classify one item at a time with immediate feedback; first-attempt scoring
keyQuestions: Is the tactic aimed at the thinking mind, the feeling mind, or the situation?
commonMisconceptions: Giving people information is always enough.
Emotion is an obstacle to change.
Changing the environment is not really leading.
assessmentOpportunities: "Fix the single sign-on so the login works on the first try." Which part does it serve?
Is a vivid picture of the destination aimed at feelings?
Why is shaping the path still leadership?

controls.name: Category buttons
controls.description: Choose the part for the current tactic.

controls.name: Submit
controls.description: Checks the choice. Two tries per tactic; only the first counts.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: Moves to the next tactic. Finish shows the score.

controls.name: Start over
controls.description: Reshuffles and begins a new run.
